# Translated motif copies

Use this branch when a noisy grid has a distinctive single-color motif amid zeros and another background color, and the demonstrations suggest translated copies of the motif are completed.

1. Record the motif's colored-cell offsets from its bounding box. Search legal translations whose motif positions all contain zeros, recoloring only those matching positions with the motif color.
2. Preserve every other cell, including the original motif and zeros or background at non-motif positions inside the bounding box. Do not assume flood-fill or neighbor propagation; test translations when the grid looks like noisy background plus one seed object.
3. Verify seed shape and legal translations against every demo's changed and unchanged cells. Allow rotation or reflection only if demonstrations support it.

# Separator tile summary

Use this branch when full-width and full-height separator lines partition a grid into equal tiles and the output dimensions match the tile layout.

1. Map each tile to one output cell. Use demonstrations to identify the in-tile feature or count that determines that cell; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive.
2. For the demonstrated pattern with color-8 separators and 2×3 tiles containing mostly color 3 and occasional color 2, emit 1 for a tile with at least two 2s and 3 otherwise.
3. Check the tile rule against every demonstrated output.

# Diagonal periodic stripes

Use this branch when sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field may specify a periodic color pattern filling the whole grid.

1. Identify the diagonal invariant: row−column is constant on down-right diagonals; row+column is constant on down-left diagonals. With zero-based row and column coordinates, use `column−row` as the down-right phase and `row+column` as the down-left phase. Check the sign convention against the demonstrations.
2. Infer the smallest plausible period by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue. Use demonstrated output to establish the complete color-per-phase mapping when available; marker positions alone may not specify every residue.
3. Color every cell from its phase, rather than preserving only sparse markers. Verify cells on several demonstrated lines and reproduce every demonstrated output.

# Missing edge continuation

Use this branch when demonstrations show color 1 marking an absent continuation at a grid edge.

1. Compare repeated rows, bands, or motif copies to infer the expected continuation and affected cells. It may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions.
2. Color only confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells. Select repeated copies from the demonstrations, not from rightmost zeros or suffix length alone.
3. Check the candidate against every demo's changed and unchanged cells.
